column11: Section 14: Mordechai's Five Royal Garments Matching the Five Soul-Levels, Shatnez in the Girdle, and Transforming Evil on Purim The theme: The five royal garments of Mordechai corresponding to the five soul-dimensions (Naran-Chai), the linen and wool girdle reconciling the two inclinations, and Purim sweetening the bitter into "very good". Scripture enumerates five royal items for Mordechai: blue (techelet), white (chur), a crown of gold (ateret zahav), fine linen (butz), and purple wool (argaman) (Esther 8:15). These correspond to the five levels of the soul: Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, Chayah, and Yechidah.

As Joseph did: “and take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt,” curbing indulgence during abundance lest they perish in famine; instructing them to provide during abundance for the famine to follow.

column13: For the Written Torah contains broad, comprehensive mandates without intricate specific applications—merely commanding to lay tefillin and the like; whereas in the Oral Torah there exist minute specifications, definitions, and precise boundaries for every facet of a mitzvah. And this precision sprouts from Chochmah, which yearns to remain cleaving to the Blessed Name within every single detail; and there is an ordered discernment in the heart knowing when to display holy firmness outwardly, and when to conceal that inner strength deep in the heart so that it remains hidden from sight.
